analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy
key_insights: Big tech earnings drove markets more than central banks this week. Alphabet fell 12.64%, its worst day on record, after results, leaving it 9.32% down YTD. The S&P 500 fell 0.30% even though 406 index stocks advanced, and the equal weight index rose 1.21% to its highest level since August.
After the bell Amazon and Intel disappointed. Nasdaq futures were down 1.86% and S&P 500 futures down 0.89% in early trading, after the Nasdaq cash index closed down 1.38%.

Amazon Q3 net sales were $201.94bn vs $202.26bn est. Spending on property and equipment was $77bn vs $59bn est. Cloud revenue growth was a touch above expectations but did not offset capex concerns. Shares fell 7% after hours, which would leave the stock marginally down YTD if repeated in the regular session.
Intel fell 23% after hours because Q4 revenue guidance of $15-16bn missed the $17.05bn estimate. The KOSPI fell 3.99% and the Nikkei fell 2.22% in Asia.
Microsoft completed a $25bn bond offering, its first major bond issuance since 2017, and the last of the US hyperscalers to turn to debt markets this year.

The tech selloff supported Treasuries. 2yr yields fell 9.8bps to 4.60% and 10yr yields fell 8.0bps to 4.94%, both the lowest since mid-September, despite strong US data. Advance Q3 GDP was +3.4% q/q annualised vs +3.2% expected (Q2: +2.2%). Initial jobless claims were 194k vs 198k expected, and the 4-week average of 196.75k is the lowest since October 1969.
September PCE: headline +0.5% m/m and +3.6% y/y, core +0.3% m/m and +3.1% y/y, all in line with expectations. The data supported Warsh's bullish growth assessment at Wednesday's FOMC.

The ECB held rates at 2.50% as expected. Lagarde signalled a December hike as the clear baseline absent a surprise, though the press release tilted dovish. Money markets priced 84% odds of a December hike (little changed) and cut 2027 hike pricing by 10bps to 64bps by next September. DB economists see 2.75% as the likely terminal rate.
Lagarde announced plans to step down as ECB President by Feb 7. DB economists expect no major short-term effect on ECB policy. Macron will be involved in choosing the successor.

European equities rose on upbeat earnings: DAX +1.31%, CAC 40 +1.05%, Stoxx 600 +0.77%, Adidas +5.76%, Shell +2.16%. European gas futures fell 2.12% to EUR 98.59/MWh after reaching the highest level since 2022 on Wednesday, helping bonds.

Brent traded around $116.11/bbl after nearly reaching $118 overnight, having fallen to $113 on Semafor's report of White House involvement in negotiations on a temporary peace deal with Iran. The WSJ then reported a top US admiral briefed Trump on military options, and Iran's Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf said Iran would not compromise.

The BOJ held rates at 1.25% with an 8-1 vote (Takata dissented, favouring a 25bp hike). It said underlying consumer inflation has reached its 2% target. It will nearly triple the pace of ETF holdings sales from January to about ¥860bn ($5.5bn) a year. The yen strengthened 0.22% to 157.38 per dollar.
Binance suspended deposits and withdrawals after a suspected hack. Bitcoin was down 0.40% this morning after a 3.03% fall yesterday.

Today brings October flash inflation for France, Spain, Germany and Italy. DB expects Euro Area HICP to rise to 3.90% y/y in October (3.77% prior) with core at 2.5%. The US Q3 employment cost index and ExxonMobil and Chevron earnings are also due.

Intel Q4 revenue guidance $15-16bn vs $17.05bn consensus est. Shares fell 23% after hours.

Adidas rose 5.76% and Shell rose 2.16% after upbeat earnings.
ExxonMobil and Chevron report earnings today.

Oil is volatile on US-Iran headlines, with a range of $113 to almost $118 in 24 hours.

crypto_views: Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, suspended deposits and withdrawals after a suspected hack. Bitcoin fell 0.40% this morning after a 3.03% fall yesterday.
risk_factors: Rising capex spending by hyperscalers (Amazon $77bn vs $59bn est.) and the souring tech mood.
US-Iran escalation risk, with Brent near $116.
Binance hack and exchange withdrawal suspension.
Higher energy costs and euro area inflation, with HICP expected at 3.90% y/y.
vol_and_positioning: The Hang Seng rose 1.75%, apparently a short covering rally in stocks that had funded the AI rotation trade.
The S&P equal weight index rose 1.21% to its highest level since August while the cap-weighted S&P fell, showing a concentrated tech-led selloff.
geopolitical: US-Iran: Semafor reported White House involvement in talks on a temporary peace deal, the WSJ reported a top US admiral briefed Trump on military options, and the WSJ reported Vice President Vance reached out to Iran's top security official to revive talks. Iran's Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf said Iran would not compromise on its position for ending the conflict.
Lagarde's early exit from the ECB lets Macron, rather than the next French president, take part in choosing her successor.
Lagarde said she was leaving early to have the freedom to speak on matters beyond monetary policy, and this opens the door to a role in the French election campaign.

tension_points.bull_case: Lagarde signalled that 'the direction of travel' is towards another hike in December, with a hike as the clear baseline absent a surprise, and money markets price 84% odds.
tension_points.bear_case: The press release tilted dovish, saying underlying inflation has been broadly stable and tighter financial conditions are likely to weigh on inflation and growth. Lagarde called yesterday a 'no hiking decision' and the ECB can wait for more information.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A surprise in data over the next six weeks that changes the December baseline.
